::: {.role}
Incoming Assistant Professor · Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, University of Rochester
:::

```{=html}
<h1 class="hero-title">Measuring greenhouse gases from space, and checking the measurements.</h1>
```

::: {.lede}
I work on atmospheric remote sensing, greenhouse gas retrievals and radiative transfer, and on the mathematics that connects satellite radiances to surface fluxes. I lead the [Environmental Remote Sensing Lab (ERSeLab)](https://erselab.github.io) at the University of Rochester.
:::


## Explore

- [Research](research/index.qmd): greenhouse gas retrievals, validation, radiative transfer, and flux inversions.
- [Teaching](teaching.qmd): EESC 222 / 422, Environmental Remote Sensing.
- [Publications](publications.qmd): journal articles and preprints on satellite retrievals, GeoCarb, and carbon cycle inversions.
- [ERSeLab](https://erselab.github.io): the lab's projects, people and results.
- [Contact](contact.qmd)

## Background

I studied mathematics at the University of Science and Arts of Oklahoma, then at the University of Oklahoma, where I earned my PhD. Along the way I found atmospheric science and the way the Earth system fits together, and I have worked on it since.
